mainTopic: Passing a husband's גט instructions through agents, and a גט given 'if I die': אביי on 'מהיום,' and רב הונא's requirement of חליצה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about a husband who sends his instructions for a גט through agents. The גמרא first splits the משנה: the רישא follows רבי מאיר and the סיפא follows רבי יוסי, who holds that spoken instructions (מילי) cannot be passed on to an agent, not even when the husband says 'Tell the scribe.' רב אשי instead reads the whole משנה as רבי יוסי, and a ברייתא backs him up: the scribe and witnesses must hear the husband's own voice. A new משנה then teaches that a גט meant to work 'if I die' or 'after death' is worthless. 'From today if I die' is valid, and 'from today and after death' is a doubtful גט. אביי explains that 'אם מתי' can mean two things, and the word 'מהיום' decides which. רב הונא rules that even with plain 'אם מתי' the widow must do חליצה. The גמרא explains that he follows רבי יוסי, for whom the date on a document shows when it takes effect. When challenged on why חליצה would then be needed, the גמרא proves through a story that רב הונא knew the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, and it begins a new answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The later clause follows רבי יוסי: spoken instructions cannot be passed on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the open question by saying this clause follows רבי יוסי, who holds that verbal instructions cannot be handed over to an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the opinion of רבי יוסי, who says: verbal instructions cannot be handed over to an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why this clause of the משנה does not worry that the scribe signed without the husband's say-so. The answer is that this clause follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, an agent who only received spoken words from the husband cannot pass them on to someone else. If the instructions cannot be passed on in the first place, the problem of a scribe acting on second-hand words never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: Words: here, spoken instructions (as opposed to a physical object like a written גט)
Cannot be handed over
An agent who acts on someone else's behalf

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule מילי לא מימסרן לשליח is the key idea for the rest of this sugya. Both readings of the משנה depend on how far רבי יוסי takes it.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yosei,
who says: words cannot be handed over to an agent.
phrases.notes: 'Words' here means the husband's spoken instructions. The agent cannot pass them along to someone else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section about why the later clause has no worry about the scribe.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the clause to a specific תנא (רבי יוסי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the clause should worry that the scribe acted without the husband's permission.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since this clause follows רבי יוסי, spoken instructions cannot be passed on at all, so that worry does not apply.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יוסי rejects even 'Tell the scribe'
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוסי allowed a husband to say 'Tell a scribe,' it would lead to a real danger. So he must reject even that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose you think רבי יוסי agrees that saying 'Tell' works. Then a problem would come out of it. Sometimes a husband says to two people, 'Tell a scribe to write, and tell so-and-so and so-and-so to sign.' Because the scribe would be embarrassed, the agents worry about him and have him sign as one of the witnesses. But the husband never said that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוסי must hold that even 'Tell a scribe' does not work. Otherwise the agents could easily end up with a גט signed by the wrong witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband named two specific witnesses. The scribe may feel insulted that he was not trusted to sign, so the agents might let him sign in place of one of them, against the husband's instructions. Since the משנה shows no worry about this, רבי יוסי must not accept 'Tell' at all. That supports the claim from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind: introduces an idea the גמרא is about to show is wrong
Agrees, concedes
'Tell' (plural command): the husband telling the agents to pass his words on to a scribe
Literally 'ruin'; here, a harmful result
Embarrassment, shame

steps.confusionAlert: The scribe is not doing anything sneaky. The danger is that the agents, trying to spare the scribe's feelings, swap him in as a witness, and the husband never authorized that.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that Rabbi Yosei agrees in a case where one says "Tell,"
a ruinous result will come out of it –
for sometimes he says to two people:
"Tell a scribe and he will write,
and tell so-and-so and so-and-so and they will sign";
and because of the embarrassment of the scribe –
phrases.notes: The scribe might feel hurt: 'Am I not good enough to be a witness?'

phrases.english: they are concerned and have him sign,
phrases.notes: The agents let the scribe sign together with one of the named witnesses, instead of both named witnesses.

phrases.english: and the husband did not say so.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּאוֹמֵר ״אִמְרוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 by showing that רבי יוסי's rule must also cover the case of 'Tell.'
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי does not accept even 'Tell a scribe' (אמרו).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A practical argument: accepting אמרו would lead to the scribe being swapped in as a witness without the husband's permission, and the משנה shows no worry about that.

steps.title: Conclusion: the first clause is רבי מאיר, the later clause is רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יוסי rejects even 'Tell,' the earlier clause cannot be his. The משנה is split between two תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: the first clause follows רבי מאיר, and the later clause follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question of authorship. The משנה has two authors: the רישא follows רבי מאיר and the סיפא follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא allows the husband's instructions to be passed on, and step 2 proved that רבי יוסי never allows that. So the רישא must belong to רבי מאיר, while the סיפא stays with רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, it is clear': the גמרא settles on an answer, often one it was hoping to avoid
The first clause of a משנה
The later clause of a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: First answer: the משנה is split. The רישא follows רבי מאיר, and the סיפא follows רבי יוסי, who holds מילי לא מימסרן לשליח even when the husband said 'Tell.'

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear:

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: the first clause is Rabbi Meir and the latter clause is Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the proof in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is split between two authors: the רישא follows רבי מאיר and the סיפא follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רב אשי: the whole משנה is רבי יוסי, building up step by step
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the entire משנה as רבי יוסי, in a 'not only this, but even that' style. Even 'Give,' even three people, and even 'Tell' do not let spoken instructions pass on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: the whole משנה is רבי יוסי, and it speaks in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say the case where he did not say 'Give'; even if he said 'Give,' it does not work. There is no need to say the case where he did not speak to three people; even if he spoke to three, it does not work. There is no need to say the case where he did not say 'Tell'; even if he said 'Tell,' it also does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different approach. The משנה does not have to be split, because the whole thing can follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי reads the משנה as climbing a ladder of stronger and stronger cases. Each case might seem strong enough to let the instructions pass on: saying 'Give,' speaking to three people, saying 'Tell.' For רבי יוסי, none of them works. So nothing in the משנה conflicts with רבי יוסי, and there is no need to bring in רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it: the entire משנה
'It speaks in a no-need-to-say style': building from an obvious case to a less obvious one
'Give': the husband telling the agents to give the גט to his wife
To three people

steps.whatToRemember: Two approaches: (1) the משנה is split between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי; (2) רב אשי says it is all רבי יוסי. For him, even 'Give,' even three people, and even 'Tell' cannot pass spoken instructions to another agent.
steps.confusionAlert: In a 'לא מיבעיא' structure, the 'even' cases are the main point. רב אשי is saying the גט fails even in the strongest-looking cases, not only in the weak ones.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
All of it is Rabbi Yosei,
and it is speaking in a "no need to say" style:
phrases.notes: He means the משנה builds up: 'not only in the easy case, but even in the harder case.'

phrases.english: No need to say where he did not say "Give,"
but even if he said "Give" – no.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא הֵיכָא דְּלָא אֲמַר לְבֵי תְלָתָא,
phrases.english: And no need to say where he did not speak to three people,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ אֲמַר לְבֵי תְּלָתָא – לָא.
phrases.english: but even if he spoke to three people – no.
And no need to say where he did not say "Tell,"
but even if he said "Tell" – also no.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading from the split-author conclusion in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the structure of the משנה ('לא מיבעיא') so that one author covers all of it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier clause seemed to allow passing on instructions, which forced us to assign it to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read as 'לא מיבעיא,' every clause says the instructions cannot be passed on, so the whole משנה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a גט is void unless the scribe and witnesses hear the husband's own voice telling them to write and sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רב אשי: even if a scribe wrote the גט for her and witnesses signed it for her, and it was given to the husband and he gave it to her, the גט is void. It only works if they hear his voice telling the scribe 'Write' and the witnesses 'Sign'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב אשי's reading from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said רבי יוסי does not allow the husband's instructions to be passed along, not even through 'Tell the scribe.' The ברייתא demands that the scribe and witnesses hear the husband himself. Any passed-along message, including 'Tell', fails.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with his view
For her sake: written specifically for this woman
Void, has no effect
His voice

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with רב אשי:
If a scribe wrote the גט for her sake
and witnesses signed it for her sake,
even though they wrote it and signed it
and gave it to him, and he gave it to her,
the גט is void,
unless they hear his voice
saying to the scribe, "Write"
and to the witnesses, "Sign."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's answer from step 4
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that for רבי יוסי even 'Tell the scribe' does not work
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא requiring that the scribe and witnesses hear the husband's own voice

steps.title: What 'they hear' and 'his voice' rule out
steps.stepSummary: 'They hear' rules out the view that רבי יוסי allows 'Tell'; 'his voice' rules out רב כהנא's ruling in the name of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'they hear' rules out the person who said רבי יוסי agrees when the husband says 'Tell.' The word 'his voice' rules out what רב כהנא said in the name of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads two words in the ברייתא closely and shows that each one rules out a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They hear' means the scribe and witnesses must hear him themselves, so a message passed along through 'Tell' is not enough. This rejects the earlier idea that רבי יוסי allows 'Tell.' 'His voice' means spoken words, which rejects the ruling רב כהנא reported in the name of רב, that written instructions are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to rule out
Agrees, concedes
'Tell!': the husband asks people to pass his message to the scribe

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, the scribe and witnesses must hear the husband's own spoken words. A passed-along message does not work, and neither do written instructions.

phrases.english: "They hear":
this rules out the one who said
that רבי יוסי agrees when the husband says, "Tell."
"His voice":
this rules out what רב כהנא said in the name of רב.
phrases.notes: רב כהנא, quoting רב, held that written instructions are enough. The word 'voice' means he must actually speak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws precise conclusions from the wording of the ברייתא in step 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The instructions must be spoken by the husband and heard directly. Both 'Tell' and written instructions are rejected.

steps.title: A גט 'if I die' versus 'from today if I die'
steps.stepSummary: A גט meant to work only at or after death is worthless. 'From today if I die' is a valid גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'This is your גט if I die,' or 'from this illness,' or 'after death,' his words mean nothing. If he says 'from today if I die' or 'from now if I die,' it is a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches which wordings work when a husband gives a גט connected to his death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט can only take effect while the husband is alive, so a גט meant to start at or after death does nothing. When he says 'from today' or 'from now,' his death only confirms a divorce that began back at the moment he spoke, while he was alive.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of a new משנה
He said nothing: the words have no effect
From today
From now

steps.confusionAlert: 'If I die' and 'from today if I die' sound almost the same, but they are opposites. Adding 'from today' makes the גט start while he is alive, so it is valid.

phrases.english: משנה:
"This is your גט if I die";
"This is your גט from this illness";
phrases.notes: He means: if I die from this illness.

phrases.english: "This is your גט after death":
he has said nothing.
"From today, if I die";
"From now, if I die":
this is a valid גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט meant to take effect at or after death is worthless. One that starts 'from today/now if I die' is valid.

steps.title: 'From today and after death' is a doubtful גט
steps.stepSummary: 'From today and after death' is a doubtful גט. If he dies, she does חליצה and may not do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'from today and after death,' it is a גט and not a גט. If he dies, she does חליצה but may not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a mixed wording and rules that it is a doubt, then explains how to act if the husband dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know whether he meant 'from today,' which makes it valid, or 'after death,' which makes it worthless. Because of this doubt, she must do חליצה in case she is still married. She may not do יבום in case she is divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: A גט and not a גט: a doubtful divorce
She does חליצה, the release from the brother-in-law
Marries the brother-in-law through יבום

steps.whatToRemember: A doubtful גט is treated strictly both ways: חליצה is needed, and יבום is forbidden.

phrases.english: "From today and after death":
it is a גט and it is not a גט;
and if he dies,
she does חליצה but does not do יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a mixed wording
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'From today and after death' is a doubtful גט, so she does חליצה and may not do יבום.

steps.title: The man who recovered from his illness and then died
steps.stepSummary: A man says 'This is your גט from today if I die from this illness.' He gets up and walks in the market, then gets sick and dies. The court assesses which illness killed him. If it was the first illness, the גט is valid. If not, it is not a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man said 'This is your גט from today if I die from this illness,' then got up and walked in the market, and later got sick and died, we assess him. If he died from the first illness, it is a valid גט. If not, it is not a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of death-conditioned גיטין with a tricky case. The man seemed to recover but later died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His condition was specific: 'if I die from THIS illness.' Walking in the market suggests he recovered, so the court must judge whether the death came from the original illness or a new one. The גט stands or falls on that judgment, because the condition is only fulfilled if the first illness killed him.

keyTerms.meaning: We assess him: the court judges the medical facts
Illness
Market; walking there shows he looked healthy
The first illness, the one named in his condition

phrases.english: "This is your bill of divorce from today,
if I die from this illness,"
and he got up and walked in the market,
and then became ill and died –
we assess him,
if he died because of the first illness –
this is a valid bill of divorce,
and if not – it is not a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ מֵהַיּוֹם, אִם מַתִּי מֵחוֹלִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of גיטין tied to the husband's death, now with a condition about a specific illness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the condition names a specific illness, the court assesses the cause of death. The גט is valid only if the first illness killed him.

steps.title: Does 'if I die' mean 'after death' or not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes a contradiction in the משנה. Plain 'אם מתי' is treated like 'after death,' so the גט is void. Yet 'from today if I die' and 'from now if I die' are valid, as if 'אם מתי' is not 'after death.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It seems that 'if I die' is like 'after death.' But then the משנה teaches that 'from today if I die' and 'from now if I die' are valid. So it seems 'if I die' is not like 'after death'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה from within. It says the same words, 'אם מתי,' seem to be treated two opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה said 'This is your גט if I die' accomplishes nothing, which treats 'אם מתי' as 'after death.' Then it validates 'from today if I die,' which treats the same words as a condition, not as 'after death.' The גמרא wants to know which reading of 'אם מתי' is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently; this shows that
Is similar to; is considered like
And then it teaches
From now

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the word 'מהיום.' The גמרא is asking how the same words 'אם מתי' can mean 'after death' in one line and not in the next.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Apparently, "if I die"
phrases.notes: This refers to the earlier line of the משנה: 'This is your גט if I die,' which it said accomplishes nothing.

phrases.english: is considered like "after death,"
and then it teaches: "From today if I die";
"From now if I die" –
apparently "if I die"
is not considered like "after death"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא ״אִם מַתִּי״ כִּ״לְאַחַר מִיתָה״ דָּמֵי, וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by pointing out an internal contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The meaning of 'אם מתי' in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same phrase is treated as 'after death' (void) in one clause and as a valid condition in the next clause.

steps.title: אביי: 'If I die' can mean two things
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that 'אם מתי' can be read two ways. It can mean 'from now' (a condition), or it can mean 'after death.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'If I die' can mean two things. It can mean the same as 'from now,' and it can mean the same as 'after death.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. He says the phrase is not fixed in one meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אם מתי' had only one meaning, the משנה would contradict itself. אביי says the words are ambiguous: they can be a condition that works from now, or they can mean the גט only starts after death. So the two clauses of the משנה do not clash. They are two readings of the same words.

keyTerms.meaning: Two meanings; two ways of reading
It means; it can be understood as
If I die

phrases.english: Abaye said:
"If I die" – it means two things;
it can mean like "from now,"
and it can mean like "after death";

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: ״אִם מַתִּי״ – שְׁתֵּי לְשׁוֹנוֹת מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ambiguity of language: the phrase carries two possible meanings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אם מתי' has one fixed meaning, so the משנה contradicts itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אם מתי' can mean either 'from now' or 'after death,' so both clauses can be true.

steps.title: Saying 'from today' decides the meaning
steps.stepSummary: אביי completes his answer. If the husband added 'מהיום,' it is like saying 'from now,' and the גט works. If he did not say 'מהיום,' it is like saying 'after death,' and the גט is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said to her 'from today,' it is like one who said 'from now.' If he did not say 'from today,' it is like one who said 'after death.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי applies his two-meanings idea to the two clauses of the משנה. This shows exactly which word tips the meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מהיום' removes the ambiguity in favor of a condition that starts now, so the גט is valid. Without it, we read plain 'אם מתי' as 'after death.' A גט cannot start after death, so it is void. This fits both clauses of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: From today
Like one who said
After death

steps.whatToRemember: Plain 'אם מתי' is read as 'after death,' and the גט is void. 'מהיום אם מתי' is read as 'from now,' and the גט is valid. The added word 'מהיום' makes the difference.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one extra word in a גט's condition can decide whether a woman is divorced at all.

phrases.english: If he said to her "from today" –
it is like one who said to her "from now,"
if he did not say to her "from today" –
it is like one who said to her "after death."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ ״מֵהַיּוֹם״ – כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר לָהּ ״מֵעַכְשָׁיו״ דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by stating which wording leads to which meaning.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'מהיום' turns 'אם מתי' into a condition that starts now, and the גט is valid. Without it, 'אם מתי' means 'after death,' and the גט is void.

steps.title: רב הונא: She must do חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of 'This is your גט if I die,' where the משנה says he said nothing. רב הונא adds that she still must do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'This is your גט if I die' means he said nothing. רב הונא said: and she does חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a line from the משנה, and רב הונא adds a ruling to it. If the husband dies without children, the wife needs חליצה and cannot do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats plain 'אם מתי' as 'after death,' so the גט does nothing. רב הונא still worries that the גט might have worked. That is why he requires חליצה, the safe path that frees her without יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: He said nothing; his words have no legal effect
An early אמורא in Babylonia
And she does חליצה (the ceremony that frees a widow from the יבם)

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not saying the גט is valid. He is saying it is not certainly empty, so she must take the safe path of חליצה.

phrases.english: "This is your גט if I die"
He has said nothing.
רב הונא said: And she does חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion: the גמרא returns to the משנה's first case (step 7), and רב הונא adds that she must do חליצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when the משנה says 'he said nothing,' the woman must do חליצה and may not do יבום.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'he said nothing'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: the משנה clearly says the husband said nothing, so why should she need חליצה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches 'he said nothing'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב הונא. If the גט is nothing, she is a normal widow and should be allowed to do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'He said nothing' sounds like the גט is completely empty. If so, there is no doubt at all, and requiring חליצה seems to go against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
It teaches (in the משנה)

phrases.english: But it teaches "he said nothing"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling from the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'He said nothing' implies the גט has no effect at all, so she should be free to do יבום.

steps.title: 'Said nothing' only for marrying others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'he said nothing' means she cannot marry other men. She is still forbidden to the יבם because of the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He said nothing' means she is forbidden to everyone else. And she is also forbidden to the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the meaning of 'he said nothing.' The phrase only tells us the גט does not free her to marry anyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's words only rule out the גט helping her. They do not prove the גט is certainly empty. Since it might be valid, she is also kept from the יבם and needs חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: She is forbidden
To the world; to everyone else
The dead husband's brother

phrases.english: "He said nothing"
means that she is forbidden to the world;
phrases.notes: She still needs a release from the יבם before she can marry anyone else.

phrases.english: and to the יבם she is also forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by limiting what 'he said nothing' means.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He said nothing' means the גט is completely empty, so she may do יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'He said nothing' only means the גט does not free her. Because of the doubt she is also forbidden to the יבם.

steps.title: The later case implies this one allows יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the משנה only mentions חליצה in the later, doubtful cases. That suggests the first case allows full יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the later part of the משנה says she does חליצה, it implies that in the first part she may even do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new problem from the structure of the משנה. The משנה only requires חליצה in a later case, which suggests the first case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later cases, like 'from today and after death,' are doubtful, so the משנה requires חליצה there. If the first case also needed חליצה, the משנה would not single out the later ones. So the first case seems to allow יבום, against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה
The first part of the משנה
By implication; it follows that
She may do יבום

phrases.english: But since in the later part she does חליצה,
phrases.notes: The later part means the doubtful cases, like 'from today and after death' (step 8).

phrases.english: it follows that in the first part
she may even do יבום!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִדְּסֵיפָא חוֹלֶצֶת, מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא יַבּוֹמֵי נָמֵי מִיַּבְּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first answer, the גמרא brings a stronger challenge from the משנה's structure.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's requirement of חליצה in the case of plain 'אם מתי'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires חליצה only in the later case. So the first case must allow יבום.

steps.title: משנה follows the רבנן, רב הונא follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the משנה follows the רבנן. רב הונא's ruling follows רבי יוסי, who says the date on a document shows when it takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה follows the רבנן. And רב הונא ruled like רבי יוסי, who said: the date of a document proves about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops trying to fit רב הונא into the משנה. It says the משנה follows one opinion and רב הונא follows another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the רבנן, plain 'אם מתי' is 'after death,' so the גט is void and she may do יבום, as the משנה implies. רבי יוסי holds that the date written on the גט shows it was meant to work from that day. So it is as if he said 'מהיום,' and the גט takes effect, which explains why רב הונא forbids יבום. The next step asks why he would then also require חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages; the majority opinion
A תנא who disagrees with the רבנן here
The date written on a document
Proves about it; shows when it takes effect

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows the רבנן: plain 'אם מתי' means 'after death,' so the גט is void. רב הונא follows רבי יוסי: the date on the גט acts like 'מהיום,' so the גט takes effect and she may not do יבום.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to אביי (step 12): saying 'מהיום' turns 'אם מתי' into a condition. רבי יוסי says the written date does the same job even without the word.

phrases.english: Our משנה follows the רבנן;
and רב הונא, who said this, follows רבי יוסי,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: זְמַנּוֹ שֶׁל שְׁטָר מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו.
phrases.english: who said: The date of a document proves about it.
phrases.notes: Since the גט carries that day's date, it is as if the husband said 'from today.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין כְּרַבָּנַן; וְרַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second challenge by saying רב הונא and the משנה follow different תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה and the אמורא to different opinions (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא was explaining our משנה, so the משנה's implication that she may do יבום contradicts him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the רבנן. רב הונא follows רבי יוסי, for whom the date on the גט makes it like 'מהיום,' so she needs חליצה.

steps.title: If he follows רבי יוסי, why require חליצה at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer. According to רבי יוסי the גט fully works, so the woman should not need חליצה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If רב הונא follows רבי יוסי, then she should not need חליצה either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 17. Under רבי יוסי there should be no need for חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that the date on the גט shows it took effect while the husband was alive, so she is fully divorced. A fully divorced woman has no tie to the יבם at all, so she needs neither יבום nor חליצה. רב הונא's demand for חליצה does not fit רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that releases a widow from her bond to the יבם
Also, too
Should not be needed

phrases.english: If it follows Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: This refers to Step 17, where רב הונא's ruling was matched to רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: she should not need חליצה either!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, חֲלִיצָה נָמֵי לָא תִּיבְעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב הונא's ruling follows רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יוסי the גט is fully valid, so there is no bond to the יבם and no reason for חליצה.

steps.title: Suggested answer: רב הונא was unsure of the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב הונא was unsure whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, so he was strict both ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that רב הונא was unsure whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי or not,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer. Maybe רב הונא did not know whether to follow רבי יוסי, so he took the strict side of each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי is right, she is divorced and cannot do יבום. If the רבנן are right, she is a widow tied to the יבם and needs חליצה. Out of doubt, רב הונא forbids יבום and also requires חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggested answer)
He is unsure about it
The final הלכה

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: And if you will say that Rav Huna is unsure
whether the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei
or the halacha does not follow Rabbi Yosei;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the challenge in Step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Doubt leading to strictness both ways
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא's ruling seems to contradict רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps רב הונא was unsure about the הלכה and was strict according to both views.

steps.title: But was רב הונא really unsure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggested answer by questioning whether רב הונא had any doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But was he really unsure?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion. It doubts that רב הונא was unsure, and the next lines bring a story to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This short line opens a challenge, and the story that follows is its evidence. If the story shows רב הונא knew the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, the 'doubt' answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it really so? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: But is he really unsure?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested answer of Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב הונא was unsure whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story will show that רב הונא knew the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The visit to רבה בר אבוה, part one
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב נחמן visit the sick רבה בר אבוה. רב הונא asks רב נחמן to ask him whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, and promises to explain רבי יוסי's reason afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה was ill, and רב הונא and רב נחמן visited him. רב הונא told רב נחמן to ask him whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. רב נחמן said: I don't even know רבי יוסי's reason, so how can I ask the הלכה? רב הונא answered: You ask the הלכה, and I will tell you the reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the story that proves the challenge. רב הונא arranges for the question about רבי יוסי to be asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא already knows רבי יוסי's reasoning, since he promises to explain it. This shows he understood the opinion well. It sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Became ill
They went in to visit him
Ask him
The reason

phrases.english: But Rabba bar Avuh was ill,

phrases.aramaic: עוּל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַב הוּנָא וְרַב נַחְמָן;
phrases.english: and Rav Huna and Rav Nachman went in to visit him;

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Rav Huna said to Rav Nachman,
Ask Rabba bar Avuh:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אוֹ אֵין הֲלָכָה?
phrases.english: Is the halacha like Rabbi Yosei, or is it not?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לָא יָדַעְנָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: I don't know Rabbi Yosei's reason,
phrases.notes: Here רב נחמן is the one talking.

phrases.english: and I should ask him the halacha?!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתְּ בְּעִי מִינֵּיהּ הֲלָכָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: You ask him the halacha,

phrases.aramaic: וְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֲנָא אָמֵינָא לָךְ.
phrases.english: and I will tell you Rabbi Yosei's reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings evidence for the challenge in Step 20
steps.raayaObject: That רב הונא was not unsure about following רבי יוסי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the visit to רבה בר אבוה

steps.title: רב rules like רבי יוסי, and רב הונא explains why
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה reports in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. Afterward, רב הונא explains that רבי יוסי holds the date of a document shows when it takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him. He answered: רב said the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. After he left, רב הונא told רב נחמן: This is רבי יוסי's reason, because he holds the date of a document proves when it takes effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a clear ruling: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. רב הונא accepted it and knew the reason, so he was not unsure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא heard a clear ruling from רב's tradition and did not question it. So the suggestion that he doubted whether to follow רבי יוסי is disproven. This brings back the question of why he required חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what רב said
After he went out
The date of a document shows when it takes effect

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא knew the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, so 'he was unsure about the הלכה' cannot explain why he required חליצה.

phrases.english: He asked him.
phrases.notes: רב נחמן asked רבה בר אבוה.

phrases.english: He said to him, so said Rav:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.
After he left, he said to him:
phrases.notes: Once they left, רב הונא kept his promise to רב נחמן.

phrases.english: This is the reason of Rabbi Yosei –

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָסָבַר: זְמַנּוֹ שֶׁל שְׁטָר מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו!
phrases.english: that he holds: the date of a document proves when it takes effect!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אֲמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story and the proof begun in Step 21
steps.raayaObject: That רב הונא accepted the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר אבוה quoting רב, and רב הונא explaining the reasoning

steps.title: New answer: רב הונא was unsure about something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the previous answer and starts a new one: רב הונא was unsure, but about a different point. The details come on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he was unsure...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new answer with 'Rather.' It is setting up the next move, which will explain what רב הונא was actually unsure about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב הונא clearly knew the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, his doubt must be about something other than the bare הלכה. The sentence continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the old answer and gives a new one)

phrases.english: Rather, he is unsure

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 19 with a new one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא doubted whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא's doubt was about a different point, explained in what follows.
